raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #1269 (base `dev/clairlee/zaya1`). Retarget to `main` once #1269 merges.

## Summary

- Add MI325X `zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` and `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml`. All six ZAYA1-8B recipes (MI300X, MI325X, MI355X × BF16, FP8) train on mock data.
- Size `micro_batch_size` on MI300X and MI325X to the largest multiple of 8 that completes on one 8-GPU node with `rocm/primus:v26.8`, end-of-training evaluation included. `global_batch_size` is micro batch × 8, so each GPU runs one micro batch per step.
- FP8 recipes set `NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON: "0"` in their `env:` block. The runner enables Transformer Engine's Triton cast-transpose, which autotunes for every new tensor shape, and ZAYA1's expert token counts change every step. With the Triton kernel, MI325X FP8 at micro batch 64 spent 307 s on step 1 and still took 2 to 10 s per step at steps 11 to 15. With the HIP cast kernel, steps take 1.8 s from step 3 on.
- Docs: MI325X added to the support matrix (config counts updated), and a throughput section in the ZAYA1 validation note.

## Results

Recipes run as checked in: 30 steps, mock data, sequence length 128, data parallel 8, `rocm/primus:v26.8` (PyTorch 2.14.0, TE 2.17.1). Step time is the median over steps 6 to 30, tokens/s/GPU the harmonic mean, and TFLOP/s/GPU the mean. Every run finished with 0 skipped and 0 NaN iterations.

| GPU | Precision | Micro / global batch | Step time | Tokens/s/GPU | TFLOP/s/GPU | Peak memory per GPU | Tokens/s/GPU before (micro 1, global 8) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MI300X | BF16 | 128 / 1024 | 1635 ms | 10016 | 118.6 | 181 of 192 GB | 171 |
| MI300X | FP8 | 120 / 960 | 1814 ms | 8478 | 100.4 | 187 of 192 GB | 115 |
| MI325X | BF16 | 216 / 1728 | 2049 ms | 13426 | 159.0 | 249 of 256 GB | 175 |
| MI325X | FP8 | 184 / 1472 | 2118 ms | 11154 | 132.1 | 245 of 256 GB | 119 |

Next size up: MI300X BF16 136 trains but stalls in the end-of-training evaluation at 98% memory. MI300X FP8 128, MI325X BF16 224, and MI325X FP8 192 run out of memory on the fp32 logits buffer.

TFLOP/s/GPU is Megatron's analytic GPT estimate. It models neither CCA nor the alternating attention and MoE stages, so compare it only between ZAYA1 runs.

FP8 is slower than BF16 at this size. With hidden size 2048 and top-1 routing over 16 experts, the expert GEMMs are small, and the FP8 casts cost more than the faster GEMMs save.

## Not covered

- MI355X was not run. Its batch sizes stay at micro 1, global 8. Its FP8 recipe gets the same `env:` override because the Triton autotuning comes from the TE build, not the GPU.
- `PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` let MI325X FP8 fit micro batch 192 (+3% tokens/s), but MI325X BF16 224 still ran out of memory. Not adopted.

## Test plan

- [x] Each MI300X (tw011) and MI325X (fremont) recipe run as checked in, without command-line overrides: 30 steps plus validation and test evaluation
- [x] `pytest tests/unit_tests/configs/test_example_configs.py -k "zaya1 or every_backend"`: 7 passed
- [x] `pytest tests/unit_tests/megatron/transformer/zaya1`: 20 passed
- [x] `pytest tests/trainer/test_megatron_trainer.py -k zaya1`: 2 passed (BF16 and FP8 smoke tests on MI300X)
- [x] `pre-commit run` on the changed files
- [x] MI355X batch sizing

-The checked-in BF16 recipes are `examples/megatron/configs/MI300X/zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` and `examples/megatron/configs/MI355X/zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml`. Those two files are the same recipe. They train on mock data (`mock_data: true`), so they need no dataset mount. The run below used the same settings with `train_iters: 30000` on GSM8K instead of mock data.
+The checked-in BF16 recipes are `zaya1_8B-BF16-pretrain.yaml` under `examples/megatron/configs/MI300X`, `MI325X`, and `MI355X`. They train on mock data (`mock_data: true`), so they need no dataset mount. They differ only in batch size: the MI300X and MI325X recipes fill GPU memory (see [Throughput](#throughput)), and MI355X reuses the MI300X batch sizes without having been run on MI355X. The run below used micro-batch 1 and global batch 8 with `train_iters: 30000` on GSM8K instead of mock data.
 
-The FP8 recipes are `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml` in the same two directories, also on mock data. They set `fp8: hybrid` with `fp8_recipe: tensorwise`. CCA Q/K/V/O projections and expert SwiGLU GEMMs are Transformer Engine FP8 linears. The router, depthwise convolutions, RMSNorm, attention, embeddings, and the tied logits projection stay in BF16. The numbers in this note are from the BF16 run.
+The FP8 recipes are `zaya1_8B-FP8-pretrain.yaml` in the same three directories, also on mock data. They set `fp8: hybrid` with `fp8_recipe: tensorwise`. CCA Q/K/V/O projections and expert SwiGLU GEMMs are Transformer Engine FP8 linears. The router, depthwise convolutions, RMSNorm, attention, embeddings, and the tied logits projection stay in BF16. The training and parity numbers in this note are from the BF16 run.
 
 Tensorwise (current) scaling takes each FP8 scale from the tensor being cast, so FP8 is accurate from the first step of a cold start. Delayed scaling starts with an empty amax history. On the released checkpoint, a cold delayed-scaling forward scored SGLang's greedy GSM8K rollouts at Pearson r 0.72 (BF16 gives 0.98) and stayed there until training-style backward passes filled the amax history. Keep `fp8_recipe: delayed` only for runs that warm the history before the steps that matter.

+
+## Throughput
+
+The MI300X and MI325X recipes were run as checked in on one 8-GPU node with `rocm/primus:v26.8` (PyTorch 2.14.0, Transformer Engine 2.17.1): 30 steps of mock data, sequence length 128, data parallel 8, one micro-batch per GPU per step. Each micro-batch size is the largest multiple of 8 that completes the recipe, including the end-of-training evaluation. Step time is the median, tokens/s/GPU the harmonic mean, and TFLOP/s/GPU the mean over steps 6 to 30.
+
+| GPU | Precision | Micro / global batch | Step time | Tokens/s/GPU | TFLOP/s/GPU | Peak memory per GPU | Next size up |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| MI300X | BF16 | 128 / 1024 | 1635 ms | 10016 | 118.6 | 181 of 192 GB | 136 stalls in evaluation |
+| MI300X | FP8 | 120 / 960 | 1814 ms | 8478 | 100.4 | 187 of 192 GB | 128 runs out of memory |
+| MI325X | BF16 | 216 / 1728 | 2049 ms | 13426 | 159.0 | 249 of 256 GB | 224 runs out of memory |
+| MI325X | FP8 | 184 / 1472 | 2118 ms | 11154 | 132.1 | 245 of 256 GB | 192 runs out of memory |
+
+TFLOP/s/GPU is Megatron's analytic GPT estimate with ZAYA1's dimensions. It models neither CCA nor the alternation of attention and MoE stages, so compare it only between ZAYA1 runs.
+
+Memory per GPU is a fixed 74 GB (BF16) or 87 GB (FP8) for weights, gradients, sharded optimizer state, and runtime buffers, plus about 0.8 GB per sample, mostly fp32 logits over the 262k vocabulary. FP8 holds extra FP8 weight copies, so it fits fewer samples. It is also slower than BF16 here: with hidden size 2048 and top-1 routing over 16 experts, the expert GEMMs are small, and the FP8 casts cost more than the faster GEMMs save.
+
+The FP8 recipes set `NVTE_USE_CAST_TRANSPOSE_TRITON: "0"` in their `env:` block. The runner turns on Transformer Engine's Triton cast-transpose by default, and that kernel autotunes for each new tensor shape. Expert token counts change every step, so with the Triton kernel the MI325X FP8 run at micro-batch 64 spent 307 s on its first step and still took 2 to 10 s per step at steps 11 to 15, against 1.8 s with the HIP cast kernel.

+work_group: ${PRIMUS_TEAM:amd}
+user_name: ${PRIMUS_USER:root}
+exp_name: ${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME:zaya1-pretrain}
+workspace: ${PRIMUS_WORKSPACE:./output}
+
+modules:
+  pre_trainer:
+    framework: megatron
+    config: pre_trainer.yaml
+
+    # Full ZAYA1-base shape lives in zaya1.yaml (80 stages, hidden 2048).
+    model: zaya1.yaml
+    overrides:
+      wandb_project: "Primus_Pretrain"
+      stderr_sink_level: DEBUG
+
+      log_avg_skip_iterations: 1
+      log_avg_reset_interval: 10
+
+      # 30-step mock-data run for one 8-GPU node (DP=8). micro_batch_size 216
+      # is the largest multiple of 8 that completes on MI325X with
+      # rocm/primus:v26.8: it peaks at 249 of 256 GB per GPU, and 224 runs out
+      # of memory. Each sample costs about 0.8 GB, mostly fp32 logits over the
+      # 262k vocabulary. On fewer GPUs, lower micro_batch_size or num_layers
+      # (keep it even). Do not edit the model yaml to shrink the architecture.
+      train_iters: 30
+      micro_batch_size: 216
+      # One micro batch per GPU per step at DP=8.
+      # Must be divisible by micro_batch_size * data_parallel_size.
+      global_batch_size: 1728
+      seq_length: 128
+      max_position_embeddings: 4096
+
+      lr: 1.0e-5
+      min_lr: 0.0
+      lr_warmup_iters: 1
+      lr_decay_iters: null
+      lr_decay_style: cosine
+      weight_decay: 0.1
+      adam_beta1: 0.9
+      adam_beta2: 0.95
+      eod_mask_loss: true
+      init_method_std: 0.02
+
+      # Data parallel only. TP, PP, CP, EP and sequence parallel are rejected
+      # by zaya1_builder.
+      tensor_model_parallel_size: 1
+      pipeline_model_parallel_size: 1
+      context_parallel_size: 1
+      expert_model_parallel_size: 1
+      sequence_parallel: false
+      overlap_grad_reduce: false
+      overlap_param_gather: false
+      gradient_accumulation_fusion: false
+
+      # Synthetic tokens. The mock-data patch forces NullTokenizer and

+      mock_data: true
+      train_data_path: null
+      valid_data_path: null
+      test_data_path: null
+      eval_interval: 100
+      eval_iters: 8
+
+      finetune: false
+      auto_continue_train: false
+      load: null
+      no_load_optim: null
+      no_load_rng: null
+      save: null
+      save_interval: 20000
+      no_save_optim: null
+      no_save_rng: null
+      disable_last_saving: true
+      ckpt_format: torch
+
+      enable_primus_turbo: false
+      use_turbo_attention: false
+      use_turbo_grouped_gemm: false
